goals.2: Giving reasons for being late or absent

dialog.1.de.4.n: After weil the verb goes right at the end
dialog.4.de.6.n: Bescheid sagen = to let someone know
dialog.4.de.7.n: denn + main clause (verb in second place): denn wir müssen planen
grammar.0.title: weil clause: verb at the end
grammar.0.text: weil starts a subordinate clause. In it the conjugated verb goes right at the end. In the main clause the verb is in second place.
grammar.1.title: weil with different tenses
grammar.1.note: Perfekt / modal verb: two verbs at the end, with the conjugated form (habe, muss) right at the very end. Separable verb: „zu Besuch kommt“ — it doesn't split, it stays together at the end.
grammar.2.title: weil or denn?
grammar.2.rows.2.0: As an answer to a question
grammar.2.rows.2.2: denn cannot stand alone as an answer to a question
quiz.4.why: In a weil clause the verb goes at the end.
quiz.5.prompt: Which is the answer to „Warum kommst du nicht?“
quiz.5.why: The answer: Weil + the verb at the end.
quiz.6.why: weil ich verschlafen habe — in the Perfekt, haben goes at the end.
quiz.7.prompt: Where does the verb go after denn?
quiz.9.prompt: Put the sentence in order: “I am ill because I have a fever.”
quiz.9.why: weil ich Fieber habe — the verb at the end.
